Biotechnology corporation that holds the patents on biochips; Mitchell's employer, on whose mesa he killed himself. Virek tried for years to buy both. Its covert team in the Sprawl, which bombed Bobby's home and killed Lucas, was after the same stray biosoft as Virek's people.
The name on the prototype biochip cyberspace decks that Hosaka has got hold of, 'the fastest thing in the matrix'.

The name on the prototype biochip cyberspace decks that Hosaka got hold of, 'the fastest thing in the matrix'; Angie wore its logo on her t-shirt. The deck at the extraction site was among the things Webber had orders to destroy.

A make of cyberspace deck.

A console cowboy or jockey works in cyberspace through a deck, most often breaking into systems for data.
Brain-dead: killed while jacked in.
An ambitious amateur with a deck; what Bobby is.
A dealer in software.
An errand man or go-between.

Artificial intelligence. The Turing Registry watches them, to keep them from becoming too clever.

The low-income arcologies beyond Barrytown, built to feed and power themselves, with fish tanks and hydroponics. One level is a holy place of Beauvoir's people; he takes Angie and Bobby there when the siege is over.
The suburb of condos in New Jersey where Bobby has lived all his life.
The suburb of condos in New Jersey where Bobby has lived all his life. Its gangs, Gothicks and Kasuals together, have been hired to surround Jammer's club in the Sprawl.
Big Playground: the concrete expanse between Barrytown's condos and the Projects, neutral ground for the gangs in name at least.
The Barrytown condo complex where Bobby and his mother live.
The Barrytown condo complex where Bobby and his mother live. The news reports their block bombed, hours after his run gave the address away.
Barrytown gang in black leather and crests of dyed hair; Bobby is on good terms with them. The Kasuals are their enemies.

A Gothick whose face has been remade after an old film idol; there are many of them.
A user of the drug dust; dusted is high on it, and dangerous.
Film: entertainment for a screen, as against simstim.
A long-running simstim soap that Bobby's mother lives in.

Long-running simstim soap from Sense/Net that Bobby's mother lives in. Its heroine is Michele Morgan Magnum, head of Magnum AG; Vasily Suslov, her lover this season, fronts for the villainous Nakamura clan.
The public body that runs nuclear power and investigates nuclear incidents.
The public body that runs nuclear power and investigates nuclear incidents. It is looking into the blast in Arizona, where it finds too little radiation for any known warhead.
The Boston-Atlanta Metropolitan Axis: the unbroken city that runs down the east coast of North America.
Chiba City, Japan, known for its black clinics: the most advanced, and often illegal, medicine and neurosurgery there is.
Japanese for a family-owned industrial combine; in the Sprawl books, any of the multinational corporations that run the world.
The Japanese crime syndicates, the 'Sons of the Neon Chrysanthemum'.
The Japanese crime syndicates, the 'Sons of the Neon Chrysanthemum'. They owe Jammer an old favour, and he has a code that opens their back door in the matrix.
The corporation that dominates simstim entertainment and owns its stars, down to their likenesses.
The corporation that dominates simstim entertainment and owns its stars, down to their likenesses. Two years on, Angie Mitchell works there as Tally Isham's understudy.
Reclusive family clan and corporation that built and owned the orbital resort Freeside. Its two AIs were at the centre of Neuromancer.

Franco-Australian family clan that built and owned the orbital resort Freeside. In the last seven years one daughter took control, grew eccentric, and the clan's interests collapsed; Freeside has been sold.
Family clan that built and owned Freeside, now ruined. Its data cores, once the family's corporate memory, were wiped, cut loose and sold for scrap; Wigan Ludgate and Jones live in them.

Family clan that built and owned Freeside, now ruined. Its data cores were wiped, cut loose and sold for scrap; there the Boxmaker, which speaks of 'the family that funded my birth', makes its boxes out of what the clan left behind.
Orbital resort built and owned by Tessier-Ashpool, with the family's home at the tip of its spindle (the setting of the second half of Neuromancer).
Orbital resort built by Tessier-Ashpool (the setting of the second half of Neuromancer). The clan, in decline, has since sold it.
Orbital resort built by Tessier-Ashpool (the setting of the second half of Neuromancer). The clan has sold it, and had the family home cut from the spindle and towed to another orbit.
The derelict data cores of Tessier-Ashpool, adrift in orbit: once the mainframes that held the clan's corporate memory.
The derelict data cores of Tessier-Ashpool, adrift in orbit: once the clan's corporate memory, partly still alive. The Boxmaker is wired into them; Virek has just bought them.

The derelict data cores of Tessier-Ashpool, adrift in orbit: once the clan's corporate memory, partly still alive, and fed by Ludgate with software sent up from Earth. The Boxmaker is wired into them. Virek bought them just before he died.
Orbital colony founded by Rastafarian workers who would not go back down the well (from Neuromancer).
The bar in the Sprawl where the best console cowboys used to gather.
A brothel whose girls work in something close to REM sleep. Bobby Quine and Automatic Jack 'burnt' its owner's system in the story 'Burning Chrome'.
Buckminster Fuller's lightweight domes. Old, unfinished geodesics roof over parts of the Sprawl.
The Earth's gravity: 'up the well' is into orbit, 'down the well' is back to the ground.
In Tibetan belief, a thought-form given a life of its own. One explanation Jammer has heard for the things in the matrix.
The Dallas–Fort Worth Sunbelt Co-Prosperity Sphere, as it looks in cyberspace.
A former department store on Madison Avenue, now fourteen floors of market stalls. Jammer's club is at the top.
A former department store on Madison Avenue, now fourteen floors of market stalls. Jammer's club is at the top; hired gangs from Barrytown have taken over the upper floors and shut it in.
New Yen: paper money, legal to hold but used almost only for business that must leave no record.
A patch that delivers a drug through the skin.
Soft synthetic foam used for beds and padding.
A flechette pistol: it fires small darts, often drugged or poisoned.
Polycarbon is a tough structural plastic. The mimetic kind takes on the colours of whatever is around it, as camouflage.
Space sickness: the nausea and racing heart of a body newly in free fall.
Maker of costly vat-grown artificial eyes through which simstim stars record.
A mobile bomb that hunts down one person, keyed to his pheromones and the colour of his hair.
A short, coded burst of radio.
A gun that throws a projectile at enormous speed by electromagnetic force.
A gun that throws a projectile at enormous speed by electromagnetic force. The news says one, fired from a cargo blimp, destroyed the mall in Arizona.

A gun that throws a projectile at enormous speed by electromagnetic force. One, fired from a cargo blimp, destroyed the mall in Arizona: part of Conroy's plan for Virek, timed for after the jet had left, so that Hosaka would blame Maas.
A line one molecule thick: nearly invisible, immensely strong, and fine enough to cut off a finger.
The webbing that holds a passenger in an acceleration couch.
Turner's revolver: a massive Smith & Wesson Tactical in .408, with a xenon projector under the barrel and explosive rounds.
Turner's revolver: a massive Smith & Wesson Tactical in .408, with a xenon projector under the barrel and explosive rounds. When it is all over he unloads it and leaves it beside Jackie's body.
A make of automatic pistol.
Maker of military lasers.
Hosaka's yacht.
The Distrito Federal: Mexico City, where Hosaka has a compound.
A life-support tank for a body, or for parts of one.

A life-support tank. What was left of Josef Virek was kept in one in Stockholm for more than ten years, until he died.
German maker of precision devices.
German maker of precision devices. A Braun biomonitor is set into a bone in the box Virek shows Marly, which proves that the box is recent.
German maker of precision devices: the biomonitor in the first box, and the solar-powered holoprojector on which Marly studies the boxes.
A small tab that holds holograms and data, played on a holoprojector.
A small tab that holds holograms and data, played on a holoprojector. Marly's seven, one for each of Virek's boxes, end up inside the box the Boxmaker makes from her things.
Park Güell, Gaudí's park on a hill above Barcelona. Virek receives Marly in a simulation of it.
Park Güell, Gaudí's park above Barcelona. Virek's construct copies it: he receives Marly there, and Bobby falls into it from Jammer's deck.
Gaudí's unfinished church in Barcelona.
The gallery in Brussels where Virek's people interview Marly.
The underground complex beneath the glass pyramid of the Louvre, where Marly meets Alain.
A jack is a plug or its socket. To jack in is to connect one's nervous system to cyberspace or to a simstim feed, through trodes or a socket in the skull.
Unlicensed medicine: clinics, the best of them in Chiba, that sell surgery, implants and biotech outside the law.
Everything a person sees, hears, feels, tastes and smells at a given moment; it is what simstim records and plays back.
Read-only memory: fixed, recorded data that plays back but cannot change or learn.
Conventional microchips, the technology that biochips are replacing; also slang for the hardware in somebody's head.
A thin surgical tape or film, close to synthetic skin.
To fence is to sell stolen goods on; a fence is the middleman who does it.
Electroencephalogram: a recording of the brain's electrical activity.
A hired fighter, usually rebuilt with surgery and implants; a woman in the trade is a razorgirl.

A hired fighter, usually rebuilt with surgery and implants. The one in the Finn's story, who worked for a Special Forces type with a cowboy out of Chiba, is Molly, with Armitage and Case: the crew of Neuromancer.
A summary; here the digest of the news that Rudy's computer compiles.
Japanese electronics maker. The entertainment module in Bobby's mother's living room is a Hitachi.
Japan Air Lines, which flies shuttles to orbit and runs a terminus there.
Turner's trade: getting a key executive or researcher out of one corporation and delivering him to another, against the will of the first.
New Delhi, the capital of India. A slamhound catches Turner there, on a street called Chandni Chawk, in the book's first lines.
City-state in South-East Asia, where the Dutchman and his team rebuilt Turner.
Arthur Conan Doyle (1859–1930), creator of Sherlock Holmes. Turner reads him in the simulated New England boyhood in which he spends his recovery.
A card that carries a line of credit: the ordinary way of paying for anything, and one that leaves a trail.
City in Morocco, the scene of one of Turner's earlier extractions.
City in Morocco. On an earlier job there Turner and a partner drove a bus, wired by Oakey, into a hotel lobby to move an IBM man over to Mitsu-G. Sutcliffe was on IBM's security at the time.
A Japanese zaibatsu. Turner has moved people out of IBM for it.
A place outside every country's law where data can be kept and traded. Somebody once tried to run one on the oil rig, in international waters.
A Kentucky bourbon; Oakey carries a flask of it.
A Kentucky bourbon; Oakey carried a flask of it, which Turner takes from his body in the wrecked helicopter.
Japanese maker of vehicles; here of the small black helicopter that sets Turner and Conroy down on the oil rig.

Japanese maker of vehicles, among them the small black helicopters used on the Mitchell job. One, armed with a laser, attacks Turner and Angie near the Sprawl; Turner wrecks it, finds Oakey among the dead and takes it for Hosaka's.
Japanese maker of vehicles, among them the small black helicopters used on the Mitchell job. The one that attacked Turner and Angie near the Sprawl, with Oakey aboard, was Conroy's.
The Mexican state south of Arizona. The Sonora line is the border, some fifty kilometres from the Maas arcology.
A flat-topped hill with steep sides. The one that matters is in Arizona: Maas Biolabs North America, the arcology where Mitchell works, is built into it.
A flat-topped hill with steep sides. The one that matters is in Arizona: Maas Biolabs North America is built into it. Mitchell sent his daughter out from it by ultralight and stayed behind.

A flat-topped hill with steep sides. The one that matters is in Arizona: Maas Biolabs North America is built into it. Mitchell sent his daughter out from it by ultralight and then, by Conroy's account, killed himself there.
The file on Mitchell that reached Hosaka on a biosoft and is handed to Turner to study.

The file on Mitchell that reached Hosaka on a biosoft: Maas's own security record of him, which feels like the work of an AI. Turner jacks it and comes away sick, with scraps of another man's life in his head.

The file on Mitchell that reached Hosaka on a biosoft: Maas's own security record of him, which feels like the work of an AI. Its scraps of Mitchell's life keep surfacing in Turner; it is how he knows the girl's name.

The file on Mitchell that reached Hosaka on a biosoft: Maas's own security record of him. Reading it again on the way to New York, Turner sees that Mitchell's career lacks the curve of real brilliance, and that Angie was never slow.
The file on Mitchell that reached Hosaka on a biosoft: Maas's own security record of him, from which Turner worked out the bargain Mitchell made. At the end he hangs it round Angie's neck.
The extraction site: a shopping mall begun before the war and never finished, now a ruin in the Arizona desert.

The extraction site: a never-finished shopping mall in the Arizona desert. As the ultralight came in the site was attacked, and seconds after Turner's jet left a blast like a small nuclear weapon wiped it out.

The extraction site: a never-finished shopping mall in the Arizona desert, on land owned by Maas. It was wiped out seconds after Turner's jet left: by a railgun fired from a cargo blimp, the news says.

The extraction site: a never-finished shopping mall in the Arizona desert, wiped out by a railgun seconds after Turner's jet left. That was Conroy's doing, for Virek: Hosaka was meant to think that Maas had done it.

Brain surgery, and a place equipped for it. Hosaka has sent a portable neurosurgery to the extraction site: a sealed pod with three medics, who are to check Mitchell for anything Maas has planted in him.

Brain surgery, and a place equipped for it. Hosaka has sent a portable neurosurgery to the extraction site, a sealed pod with three medics who are to check Mitchell for anything Maas has planted in him. Webber has orders to put a rocket into it if the job goes wrong.

Brain surgery, and a place equipped for it. Hosaka sent a portable neurosurgery to the extraction site, a pod with three medics who were to check Mitchell over. When the site was attacked Webber fired her rocket into it, with the medics inside.
An explosive charge planted in an employee's head, so that he cannot defect and live. Hosaka's medics are to look for one in Mitchell.
A very light one-person aircraft.
A very light one-person aircraft. Mitchell is to fly out of the Maas arcology in one; the one that comes down at the mall is flown by a girl.
A very light one-person aircraft. Mitchell had only the one, and sent his daughter Angie out of the Maas arcology in it instead of going himself.
Kilometres.
A mercenary.
A Japanese assassin trained in an old tradition of stealth; loosely, any corporate killer.
A Japanese assassin trained in an old tradition of stealth; loosely, any corporate killer. Hosaka keeps its own, and it is what the Finn calls the three black-clad men he has killed in his shop.
A vehicle that rides on a cushion of air held in by a flexible skirt, the apron-bag; a 'hover' for short.
A vehicle that rides on a cushion of air held in by a flexible skirt, the apron-bag; a 'hover' for short. Rudy gives Turner his own, an armoured war-surplus machine that runs on kerosene.

A vehicle that rides on a cushion of air held in by a flexible skirt, the apron-bag; a 'hover' for short. Rudy gave Turner his armoured one; Turner rams a helicopter with it, runs it out of kerosene on the edge of the Sprawl and leaves it there.

A vehicle that rides on a cushion of air held in by a flexible skirt, the apron-bag; a 'hover' for short. Rudy's armoured one was left out of fuel on the edge of the Sprawl; when Turner walks out of Jammer's he says he has eighty litres of kerosene to buy first.
The wood near the family farm where Turner and his brother hunted squirrels as boys.
The wood near the family farm where Turner and his brother hunted squirrels as boys. Turner's jet has hidden itself there.

The wood near the family farm where Turner and his brother hunted squirrels as boys. The jet he hid there is still sinking into the loam when, years later, he brings his own son to the clearing to learn to shoot.
American make of rifle: the nylon-stocked one of Turner's boyhood squirrel hunts.
American make of rifle: the nylon-stocked one of Turner's boyhood squirrel hunts. It was Rudy's; years later Turner teaches his son to shoot with it.
The capital of Colombia.
The capital of Colombia. The jet that Conroy programmed was logged for a strip near it, not for Hosaka's compound in Mexico City.

The capital of Colombia. The jet that Conroy programmed was logged for a strip near it, not for Mexico City: having sold the job to Virek, he meant Turner and Mitchell to be there before the site was wiped out.
Swiss city where, by his dossier, Mitchell once lived with his baby daughter.
Swiss city. Angie grew up there after her father joined Maas; Turner's agent, too, is no more to him than a voice and a telephone number in Geneva.
A language grown out of a mixture of others, such as the French-based speech of Haiti. It is Rudy's guess at what Angie speaks in her trance.

A make of supercomputer. Rudy's old one compiles him a digest of the corporate news.
The scholar of German legend who sells his soul to the devil in return for knowledge and power.
The scholar of German legend who sells his soul to the devil in return for knowledge and power. The name comes to Turner when he works out what Mitchell must have done.
The code of the samurai, founded on loyalty to one's lord. 'Mr Bushido' is Conroy's sneer at Turner.
A wealthy avenue of Manhattan.
A wealthy avenue of Manhattan. Jaylene Slide says the people behind the siege of Jammer's are 'Euros', Europeans, who work from there behind very heavy ice.

A wealthy avenue of Manhattan. The 'Euros' who work from there behind very heavy ice are Virek's people, with Conroy now in charge of them; they are behind the siege of Jammer's. Jaylene Slide orders his floors destroyed.
A wealthy avenue of Manhattan, where Conroy ran Virek's people. On Jaylene Slide's order two floors of a building there are hit with incendiary shells; Conroy is almost certainly dead.
The capital of Sweden.
The capital of Sweden. What is left of Josef Virek lies in a life-support vat in one of its industrial suburbs.
The capital of Sweden. What is left of Josef Virek lies in a life-support vat in one of its industrial suburbs; Conroy promises to have Angie delivered there.
The capital of Sweden. Josef Virek lay for years in a life-support vat in one of its industrial suburbs, and has died there.
One of the airports of Paris.
One of the airports of Paris. Marly's JAL shuttle to orbit leaves from it.
Tally Isham's syndicated simstim talk show.
German for a whole that is more than the sum of its parts. Virek uses the word of himself: the thing in the vat together with everything his money has built around it.
New Melbourne: where Jones says he comes from. Marly takes his accent for Australian.
An unmanned, partly self-directing machine for building in orbit.
An unmanned, partly self-directing machine for building in orbit. The Boxmaker is one, welded into the roof of a dome and cabled into the Tessier-Ashpool cores.
Video screens that Wigan Ludgate has stuck up all over the cores, meaning to preach from them.
Video screens that Wigan Ludgate has stuck up all over the cores, meaning to preach from them. Virek, and then Paco, use the one in the Boxmaker's dome to speak to Marly.
A make of automatic pistol.
A make of automatic pistol. The child Paco draws a tiny one on Bobby in Virek's construct.
The European transit line by which Marly comes to Brussels, on a fare borrowed from Andrea.
A message or a news-sheet sent down the line and printed where it is read; 'the fax' is also the news in general.
A fashion label; Marly's one good jacket is a Sally Stanley.
A fashion label. Marly's one good jacket is a Sally Stanley, and so is the shirt of Rhea's that Bobby bleeds on.
German, 'catatonic art': the school of the stabbed sheets of cardboard on the walls of the Galerie Duperey, by now safe and conservative.
The European telephone carrier, over which an ordinary simstim link would run.
The Ramblas: the tree-lined main promenade of Barcelona.
The Dutch bank, with a branch in orbit, where Virek's people have opened an account in Marly's name.
The Quartier des Ternes: the district in the north-west of Paris where Andrea lives.
A Japanese department-store chain. Marly buys a silk blouse at its Paris branch with Virek's money.
The rue du Faubourg Saint-Honoré, the smartest shopping street in Paris; Marly has her hair cut there.
The rue du Faubourg Saint-Honoré, the smartest shopping street in Paris. Marly has her hair cut there, and the Roberts gallery stands in it.
The rue Mauconseil in Paris, where Marly had her very small gallery; she and Alain lived for a year in the room behind it.
A French brand of strong, dark cigarettes; Alain smokes them unfiltered.
A French brand of strong, dark cigarettes; Alain smoked them unfiltered. The number he hid for Marly is written on an empty packet.
A French brand of strong, dark cigarettes; Alain smoked them unfiltered. The number he hid for Marly on an empty packet is a set of orbital co-ordinates.

The shop where Marly once bought Alain his leather-bound agenda.
The shop where Marly once bought Alain his leather-bound agenda. When she finds him dead, the agenda is gone.
A Paris café with a terrace, where Marly used to spend her evenings with Alain.
The Aeschmann Collection in Hamburg, which takes only the art of psychotics.
The Aeschmann Collection in Hamburg, which takes only the art of psychotics. A year before his death Roberts became a patron of it, and applied to join the Institut de l'Art Brut in Paris.
